gate.checkstyle:
pass - and it had to be repaired first. A reformat of pom.xml joined <propertyExpansion> onto one line, which Properties.load reads as a single key; the build failed with `No enum constant SeverityLevel.WARNING PACKAGE.INFO.SEVERITY=IGNORE`. Fixed with 
 in both the root POM and ludwig-service-parent.

tests.passed: full suite, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped (integration tests included - Docker was up)

caveats: `mvn clean install` with no flags FAILS on this machine, and would have failed before this change too: there is no Docker daemon (`Could not find a valid Docker environment ... NoSuchFileException (/var/run/docker.sock)`), so every Testcontainers-backed test errors. The green build was obtained with `-Dsurefire.excludesFile=<45 Docker-dependent classes> -DskipITs`. Both flags were typed on a command line for this run only and appear in no POM, script or Jenkinsfile. The exclusion list was derived by seeding on Testcontainers/LudwigTestImages/container-configuration references and closing over subclasses.

`-Dtest='!X,!Y'` was tried first and had to be abandoned: passing -Dtest at all makes architecture-rules' JUnitIntegrationTest fail with `No base-exception type is configured`, which is a test-isolation artefact of surefire's filter rather than a defect. -Dsurefire.excludesFile does not have that effect. Recording it because the next person will otherwise repeat the experiment.

Task 3.1's own verification command, `mvn -Pci ... package`, could not be run: -Pci is denied to agents by .claude/settings.json, exactly as design.md's Context section anticipated. The Javadoc attachment was verified by invoking the goals directly instead, which is possible because the configuration lives in pluginManagement and only the <execution> is inside the profile.

gitversion.yml has never been EXECUTED. There is no Docker daemon and no .NET runtime here, so `/showvariable MajorMinorPatch` was not run. Every key and value was validated against GitVersion's published 6.0 JSON schema, which is a real check of the configuration and not a check of its output.

The -Prelease changelog rules were amended after the first hand-off: both conditions short-circuit on a SNAPSHOT version, so `mvn -Prelease` with no -Drevision now reports only requireReleaseVersion instead of three errors for one mistake. All three paths re-verified: no -Drevision gives one error, -Drevision=9.9.9 gives both changelog errors naming each locale, -Drevision=1.1.0 passes all four release rules.
retries_detail: 1.2 requirePluginVersions: three attempts. It reported four super-POM lifecycle plugins, then maven-resources-plugin for the jar modules, then maven-site-plugin for ludwig-service-parent. Resolved by pinning all five rather than by excluding them.

3.1 javadoc: three attempts at a non-delombok fix (javadoc -processorpath, a second class-path option, target/classes prepended to the classpath). All three measured and all three failed; the fourth attempt, delombok, needed a design amendment the user approved.
4.2 evaluateBeanshell: one attempt with java.nio.file.Files.readAllBytes(Paths.get(...)), which BeanShell cannot evaluate because it has no varargs. Rewritten with java.util.Scanner.
9.3 the full build: four attempts at an exclusion mechanism before -Dsurefire.excludesFile.
unresolved: 8.2 NOT DONE and blocked twice over. `mvn -Drevision=1.1.0 -Prelease -Pci -DskipTests deploy` was attempted and refused by the permission layer. Independently, it could not have worked: no ~/.m2/settings.xml, so no <server> credentials, and distributionManagement points at the placeholder https://nexus.example.internal/. The operator must supply a real -Dludwig.repo.releases.url and a settings.xml <server> entry.

8.3 NOT DONE - it needs a published baseline. The acceptance criterion (zero revapi differences against a freshly published 1.1.0) is still unmeasured. What IS measured is zero differences against an empty archive, which is a weaker statement.

8.4 DONE by the user ahead of 8.3. failBuildOnProblemsFound is true. Arming it early cost three red builds but surfaced every configuration artefact before any baseline existed, which is what 8.3 was for; the residual risk is that a difference only visible against a REAL baseline is still unseen.
gitversion.yml remains schema-valid and unexecuted. Docker is now available on this machine, so one run of the pinned container would close it.
The revapi.differences list holds two exemption entries and no per-difference removal entries. It stays that way until the first deliberate removal.

revapi_exemptions.java.missing.newClass for jakarta.servle: FIXED AT THE CAUSE, not exempted. resolveTransitiveProvidedDependencies=true. The classes were resolvable, just not resolved; revapi warns that the analysis 'may be incorrect' without them, and muting a class it could have loaded makes an incorrect analysis quiet.
revapi_exemptions.java.missing.(new|old)Class, remainder: Exempted. 23 SAML2/LDAP/OAuth2-client types declared by HttpSecurity, in jars this platform does not depend on. Absent from both archives, so never a difference between two releases.
revapi_exemptions.java.class.externalClassExposedInAPI / n: Exempted. revapi's API-design advisory family, computed from the new archive alone; fires identically on a build with no source change and would fire on a first release.
revapi_exemptions.rule for the next one: A code that compares two archives stays armed; a code computed from one archive is not a compatibility statement. Recorded in docs/harness-enforcement.md.
